newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures seen drifting lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. debt futures seen drifting lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures are expected to drift lower in a short-term correction after September T-bonds rose to a seven-month high of 114-03/32 on Wednesday.

The yield's slide towards the key psychological support level of 6.50 percent, or about 115-00 in the September T-bond futures contract, persisted this week but may have run out of momentum on Thursday, technical analysts said.

Bruce Kamich, senior vice president at MCM MoneyWatch Inc, said September bonds stalled just below an upper channel set in the last two weeks. He said the market has been operating between that recent channel and a channel from the April low.
"We've had a nice leg up, so I think the market will trade sideways to easier until late July to early August," Kamich said.
He said the correction may continue through U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on monetary policy and economic conditions on July 22.

Chris Dickerson, an analyst with Global Market Strategists Inc, also noted that the T-bond rally was mature and that futures prices were vulnerable to a selloff after Friday's U.S. producer price index data.
"If the PPI gives us something to worry about, September could fall to 111-00," Dickerson said.
So far, September T-bonds have limited losses to 113-16/32. Support is at 113-12/32 and Monday's low of 113-03/32. Further support is at 112-24/32.
However, most technical analysts agreed that the long-term picture was still bullish at least until Labor Day. Many analysts are eyeing the next major resistance level at 116-00.
"We won't make new new highs, but we will challenge the highs of December 1996," Kamich said, referring to the 1-1/3-year high of 115-17/32 set on December 3, 1996.
He said the 116-00 level is roughly equivalent to a cash long bond yield of 6.30 percent and near the upper end of a range set since 1993.
The next upward target comes near the 117-16/32 area, Dickerson said.

He said a rally to 117-16/32 would represent a C wave, according to Elliott Wave analysis, and that the breadth of such an upmove would match wave A which lifted prices from July 1996 to December 1996. Wave B started in December and took the contract to 105-30/32, a nine-month low set on April 11, 1996.
"The fundamental environment could warrant a move to 5.75 percent to 5.50 percent (U.S. long bond yield) in the longer term," Dickerson said. ((Chicago derivatives desk (312)408-8750))
